craft_claim: Prophetic and civic oratory pairs honest indictment of a present failing with a forward promise of restoration, and this two-part structure supplies the inspirational voice's characteristic rise.

supporting_evidence.location: The American Jeremiad, Introduction and chapters on the Puritan sermon
supporting_evidence.note: Bercovitch describes the American jeremiad as fusing a biblical standard, a candid naming of falling-short, and a promise of restored community, sustaining a rhetoric of hope and fear.

supporting_evidence.location: The Preacher King, chapters on King's preaching and the folk pulpit
supporting_evidence.note: Lischer shows King absorbing the cadences, parallelism, and call-and-response of the African-American folk pulpit and transposing them from sacred preaching into public address.
The address names injustice plainly before envisioning its resolution, refusing to skip the wound in the manner of the jeremiad.

counterevidence.note: Critics of the jeremiad note it can deflect systemic critique into individual renewal and thereby function as a rhetoric of social control.

scope: Civic oratory, public essay, and purpose-driven nonfiction.
exceptions: Apolitical personal-inspirational writing may use only the forward promise without the indictment half.
